I am managing by randomly googling things I think are probably important, but It would be nice if there was some kind of proper introduction to gardening somewhere out there on the internet. Any youtube channels or some kind of proper good introductory page out there?
Is there some sort of wiki or note for absolute beginners to gardening?

Wow...that's a tall order! :) Like you, I did a quick search and most of the sites go over the same information....quality of soil, amount of sunlight, amount of moisture and planning.

Better Homes and Gardens seems to be a good overview.

The YouTube channel GrowVeg seems to have a lot of good tutorials for vegetable gardening (assuming by your username that is what you are interested in).

The Farmers Almanac is always a good source of info

The Harrowsmith Northern Gardener was a favourite of mine (until I lent it out to someone never to be seen again...that bastard!). Perfect if you are in the northern climes.

And one concept that sounds soooooo good for beginning a vegetable garden is Square Foot Gardening. The easiest way to fail is to plant too much of one thing, or too much of everything. This planning method helps you keep your selections to a manageable amount, in raised boxes that are easier to maintain. I have tried very few vegetables before, and hope to try one of these boxes in the next year or two to get me going. Vegetables take a lot more care than perennial flowers. I need the help!

And finally....from my own experience...make sure you start with good soil. Add compost to any soil before you start...you can often get it free from municipalities that do green-bin type of collections. Where I live, there are a lot of mushroom farms that give it away. A good soil makes everything easier.

Then once your plants are in, mulch like your life depends on it. Mulching keeps down weeds, and holds in moisture. It will make irrigation a ton easier.

I hope these ideas help!

I’m working on it, old mod was not active and I just took over. Going to start off by putting together a newbie FAQ.

"Square Foot Gardening" by Mel Bartholomew I think is pretty good, but I've been gardening most of my life, since about age 10. Here are some general rules I use:

  • Water plants every day the temperature reaches 80F. Also check them every day, if the soil is not dry, do not water them.
  • Cucurbits (cukes, pumpkins, squash, etc) need richer soil. I don't have rich soil, it's loamy, so I fertilize them with 12-12-12 every 3 weeks. They love it.
  • Do not let cucurbits dry out. For most plants, if the leaves are droopy, they need water.
  • Mulch your plants. It slows the time needed for the soil to dry out. Especially useful in the hot summer months.

From someone who attended the event:

Re: scouting:

-Simplifying terms for the scouts so they're all "speaking the same language"

-Jim Benning's scouting background was key to his hiring (cited his track record with buffalo and Boston....I didn't get a chance to question that).

Willie has confidence in Jim to address the issues that became apparent. Didn't elaborate. Fluff answer to the question of: what did you learn from the playoff loss to Calgary.

When asked about specific prospects and where they fit in to the lineup in the next year or two: Didn't elaborate on which prospects could make the team. Just said it will be up to the players to earn their job.

NTC strategy: if you try to sign someone as a free agent you have to give them a NTC or else they won't come.

-Top players on team will be given NTC's but they won't give them out to just anyone. If they have to trade someone they will approach them about it.

-Trying to make moves going into the draft and "we will see how it goes."

-Jim says he wants to do whatever it takes to make the team better, and build a team that we want to come see.

Jim wants to keep Miller because he thinks when he is on his game he gives the team confidence. Says Miller was real good. Likes Miller's experience as a number 1 goalie and wants him to mentor one of the young goalies. Looking at options between Markstrom and Lack.

Someone questioned Miller's term and money.

Jim: he was the best free agent goalie in the market. Miller wanted more years. Organization brought him down to 3 years. Claims goalies are the highest paid players on every team. Lots of starting goalies between 5.5 to 8, and gave him the low end of what starting goalies make.

When asked who could replace Henrik?

-Sedins feel if they don't score that we won't win. They take that pressure on them. Henrik can't be replaced, but other guys will chip in and replace his scoring when he moves on.

On Kassian:

-Zack wasn't great early, played real well during a later stretch, hurt for the whole playoffs. Has lots of potential but needs to work on consistency.

Asked about term for Dorsett and Sbisa:

Willie says they're great guys for the team. Dorsett makes teammates better by making other team accountable. Believes Sbisa has big upside. "How bad do you want to be a player?" Luca is watching his shifts and studying how to get better.

Jim: Dorsett is a culture character who they want young guys rubbing elbows with. Helped develop Bo from the beginning of the year. Wants him to help confidence of younger players.

On Sbisa, after next season he is a free agent (along with Hamhuis and Bieksa). Due to lack of defenseman prospects and depth he felt it was paramount to lock him up in case we lose Hamhuis or Bieksa. Talks about how Sbisa and Dorsett lead team in hits and play with emotion to hit someone and make it exciting for the fans.

On Kassian again:

Willie doesn't believe in just giving Kassian a top 6 role. Wants him to earn it. Was pencilled in originally but his play didn't warrant it.

On defensemen depth going into the draft:

Identified lack of depth on defense for the team. Talks about Pedan acquisition, Clendening, signed Ben Hutton, Jordan Subban. Considers them all developing prospects. Definitely a concern, but didn't say if they would target one in the draft. Pointed out its been 10 years since we drafted a Dman in round 1.
